findings.issue: Match restart detection gap in getClosingSpeed()
findings.description: The first-call guard (prevT == 0) only handles initial startup. When the switch is toggled mid-session, loop() resets dodgeCount and calls feature reset functions, but getClosingSpeed() has no reset mechanism — its static variables persist. On the first call after restart, prevT might be 45000 (from the previous match) and millis() might be 48000 (3 seconds into the new match), producing a valid but incorrect dt = 3 seconds.
findings.action: Add an explicit reset function or pass a reset flag when the match restarts.

findings.description: getRollingClosingSpeed() tries to detect match restarts by checking if prevT > now + 1000 (time went backwards). This only works if the Arduino restarts and millis() resets to 0, which doesn't happen when the switch is toggled — the Uno keeps running and millis() keeps counting up. The existing resetRollingSpeed() function is called from the switch restart block but it does nothing useful — it just calls getRollingClosingSpeed(NO_DETECT_CM) hoping the time-went-backwards check will fire, which it won't.
findings.action: Change resetRollingSpeed() to explicitly zero out the static state (add a global needsReset flag or return early on a sentinel input value).
